main_body: T-shaped timber prop: a wide horizontal beam on top of a thin vertical post
top_band: orange/light-orange top surface at rows 10-12 (dark brown back edge at row 9), then a cream front-edge line at row 13
evidence: Reading down a column through the beam: row 9 dark outline, rows 10-12 light orange top, row 13 cream front-edge highlight, rows 14-16 darker brown front face with a slightly darker band beneath the edge, row 17 dark base line. The beam has a readable top surface, a distinct edge line and a front face, close to the guide's 'seat top + edge' pattern. The post below is a plain vertical shaft and is covered at its top by the beam. The top is thin at 3 rows but real, so this passes narrowly.

style.evidence: The beam carries about 5 tones (dark brown, orange, light orange, cream, mid brown) with a few speckle dots, and the outline is a tinted dark brown rather than black. The long post is only 3-4 tones: a narrow light stripe, one knot band and dark sides, with little grain. Its tiles hold far fewer colours than the stall and well references, so the piece reads thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard.
